title: SPARC: Reliable Spatial Annotations from Robot Demonstrations at Scale
title_zh: SPARC：从大规模机器人演示中获取可靠空间标注
abstract_en: This work introduces Spatial Annotations from Robot Demonstrations with Reliability Calibration (SPARC), a risk-aware framework that automatically labels robot demonstrations with structured spatial annotations and assigns each annotation a reliability score. Structured spatial annotations, such as bounding boxes, object trajectories, and manipulation phase labels, benefit a broad range of robotics applications from training grounded robot policies and embodied foundation models to motion planning and hierarchical task composition. Existing automated pipelines generate such annotations at scale but provide no reliable quality signal: detector confidence is poorly calibrated for annotation correctness, forcing a choice between accepting noisy labels or discarding useful samples. In contrast to existing automated pipelines, SPARC leverages the spatio-temporal structure inherent to robot tasks to generate a reliability signal, reducing noisy labels and retaining more useful samples. We further introduce Interaction-Aware Bench (IA-Bench), a benchmark that measures model accuracy in grounding the locations of interacted objects in robot demonstrations. On 1.7k human-annotated demonstrations spanning diverse embodiments and scenarios, SPARC significantly outperforms detection-only baselines in localization accuracy while retaining three times more samples at high-precision operating points. Our experiments demonstrate that models finetuned on our annotations achieve state-of-the-art results on object-grounding and pointing benchmarks among similarly sized models, while remaining competitive on broader spatial-reasoning suites without manually verified or annotated training data. Furthermore, policies trained on SPARC-generated annotations outperform baselines in cluttered, visually ambiguous real-world scenes. Code, data, and models are available at intuitive-robots.github.io/sparc-labeling.
abstract_zh: 本文提出 SPARC（Spatial Annotations from Robot Demonstrations with Reliability Calibration），一个风险感知框架，可自动为机器人演示生成结构化空间标注，并为每个标注分配可靠性分数。此类标注包括 bounding boxes、object trajectories 和 manipulation phase labels，可用于训练 grounded robot policies、embodied foundation models，以及支持 motion planning 和 hierarchical task composition。现有自动化流水线虽能大规模生成标注，但缺乏可靠的质量信号；检测器置信度与标注正确性校准较差，导致用户只能在接受噪声标签和丢弃有用样本之间取舍。SPARC 利用机器人任务中的时空结构生成可靠性信号，从而减少噪声标签并保留更多有用样本。作者还提出 Interaction-Aware Bench（IA-Bench），用于评估模型在机器人演示中定位被交互物体的 grounding 能力。在覆盖多种机器人形态和场景的 1.7k 人工标注演示上，SPARC 相比仅检测基线显著提升定位准确率，并在高精度工作点保留 3 倍更多样本。实验表明，使用 SPARC 标注微调的模型，在同等规模模型中于 object-grounding 和 pointing benchmarks 上达到 state-of-the-art，同时在更广泛的 spatial-reasoning 测试中保持竞争力，且无需人工验证或人工标注训练数据。基于 SPARC 标注训练的策略在杂乱、视觉歧义的真实场景中也优于基线。
key_points_zh: 提出 SPARC，为机器人演示自动生成 bounding boxes、object trajectories、manipulation phase labels 等结构化空间标注，并为每个标注估计可靠性分数。
核心思想是利用机器人任务的时空结构进行可靠性校准，而非依赖未充分校准的 detector confidence，从而在降低噪声的同时保留更多有效样本。
提出 Interaction-Aware Bench（IA-Bench），专门评估模型在机器人演示中定位被交互物体的能力。
在 1.7k 人工标注演示上，SPARC 相比 detection-only baselines 显著提升定位精度，并在高精度设定下保留约 3 倍样本。
使用 SPARC 标注微调的模型在 object-grounding 和 pointing benchmarks 上达到同规模模型 SOTA，并能提升真实杂乱场景中的机器人策略表现。

llm_assessment.comment: SPARC tackles an important data-quality bottleneck in robot demonstrations with reliability-calibrated spatial annotations, likely offering practical value despite moderate conceptual novelty.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: SPARC通过可靠性校准的空间标注解决机器人示教数据质量瓶颈，概念创新中等但实用价值较高。
